description: issue #768, the COMPOUND half of the rule: a `list` prompt raises `ol-type` (`spec/interaction-events.md:186`/`:188` — the prompt MUST be a `word`). This was already rejected before the ruling; what changed is `params.expected`, which moves from #681's one-off `"text"` to `"word"`, so every "this argument must be text" diagnostic in OpenLogo now carries one identity (the `word` reporter's, and the profile's own `when`/`on_key`). `list` stands for the four compound/opaque kinds because all four fail the same single type test; `dict` and `record` would additionally require the Data profile and `turtle` the Sprites one, coupling an Interaction fixture to profiles it does not depend on for no extra proof, so those three stay under `packages/runtime/src/interaction-input.test.mjs`, which asserts all six rejected kinds in one loop. The bracketed argument also confirms the reader takes `[ 1 2 ]` after a Kind-R reporter as a LIST literal, not as a block: a block would not reach the prompt check at all.
